textbook_title: Mastering Coding: AI and Robotics — Level 3

source.title: Mastering Coding: AI and Robotics — Level 3
source.note: Chapter and topic structure follows the updated Teacher Panel curriculum. Topic explanations, learning points and activities are adapted lesson notes, not verbatim textbook transcription. Consult the linked textbook PDF for complete original text, diagrams and exercises.

chapters.title: The Computer System
chapters.description: Explore the computer system through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: A computer system accepts data and instructions as input.
The processing unit works on the input.
Desktop computers are commonly used at a fixed workstation.
Laptops are portable computers.

topics.title: What is a Computer System?
topics.content: A computer system is an electronic system that accepts input, processes data, stores information and produces output. The chapter introduces the main parts that work together to perform these tasks.
learning_points: A computer system accepts data and instructions as input.
The processing unit works on the input.
The system produces useful information as output.
Different computer devices use the same basic input, process and output idea.
examples: Processing: Work on the supplied data.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to identify the input, processing and output parts in a desktop computer.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Types of Computers
topics.content: The textbook introduces different computer types, including desktops, laptops, tablets and other compact or specialised computers. Their form and size vary according to how and where they are used.
learning_points: Desktop computers are commonly used at a fixed workstation.
Laptops are portable computers.
Tablets and smartphones are compact computing devices.
Special-purpose computers are built into many everyday systems.
examples: Desktop: Usually stays at a workstation.
topics.activity_text: Show pictures of a desktop, laptop, tablet and smartphone. Ask students to compare portability and use.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Input Devices
topics.content: Input devices help users enter data and instructions into a computer. The chapter shows common input devices and explains how they help people communicate with a computer.
learning_points: A keyboard enters letters, numbers and commands.
A mouse or touchpad controls the pointer.
A microphone captures sound.
A scanner and camera can send images into a computer.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to sort the pictured devices into keyboard, pointing, sound and image input.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Output Devices
topics.content: Output devices present the results of computer processing. They communicate information through visual, printed or audio output.
learning_points: A monitor displays text, pictures and video.
A printer produces a paper copy.
Speakers and headphones provide sound output.
A projector displays computer output on a large screen.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to name whether a monitor, printer, speaker or projector produces visual, printed or audio output.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Processing Devices
topics.content: Processing devices work on the data and instructions entered into a computer. The CPU is the main processing component described in the chapter.
learning_points: The CPU stands for Central Processing Unit.
It processes data and follows instructions.
Processing turns input data into useful information.
topics.activity_text: Use the input–process–output sequence to explain what happens when a student types a word and sees it on screen.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Storage Devices
topics.content: Storage devices keep data, programs and information so they can be used later. The chapter introduces examples of storage hardware.
learning_points: A hard disk or solid-state drive stores files in a computer.
A pen drive is portable storage.
Memory cards store files in compact devices.
Optical discs are another storage medium.
examples: Hard disk: Stores files inside a computer.
Optical disc: Stores data on a disc.
topics.activity_text: Ask students which storage device they would use to carry a school presentation to another computer.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

chapters.title: Hardware and Software
chapters.description: Explore hardware and software through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: The monitor, keyboard, mouse and CPU cabinet are hardware.
Hardware components work together as a computer system.
Keyboard, mouse and scanner are examples of input hardware.
Monitor, printer and speakers are examples of output hardware.

topics.title: Computer Hardware
topics.content: Hardware means the physical parts of a computer that can be seen and touched. The chapter groups hardware according to the work each part performs.
learning_points: The monitor, keyboard, mouse and CPU cabinet are hardware.
Hardware components work together as a computer system.
Different hardware components perform input, processing, output or storage tasks.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to point to five hardware parts in the computer lab and describe their purpose.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Input, Output and Storage Hardware
topics.content: Computer hardware can be grouped by function. Input hardware sends data into the computer, output hardware presents results, and storage hardware keeps data.
learning_points: Keyboard, mouse and scanner are examples of input hardware.
Monitor, printer and speakers are examples of output hardware.
Hard disks, pen drives and memory cards are storage hardware.
examples: Input: Sends data to a computer.
topics.activity_text: Create three labels—Input, Output and Storage—and ask students to place device names under the correct label.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Computer Software
topics.content: Software is the set of programs and instructions that tells computer hardware what to do. Hardware and software work together to make a computer useful.
learning_points: Software consists of programs and instructions.
A computer needs software to perform tasks.
The chapter groups software into system, application and utility software.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to name software they use for drawing, writing or learning.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: System Software
topics.content: System software helps operate and control the computer. An operating system manages the computer and provides an environment in which applications can run.
learning_points: System software helps the computer work.
An operating system manages computer resources.
Windows and Linux are examples shown in the textbook.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to identify the operating system they see when the computer starts.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Application Software
topics.content: Application software helps users perform particular tasks, such as writing, drawing, learning or playing games.
learning_points: Word-processing software is used to create documents.
Drawing programs help users create pictures.
Educational programs support learning.
Different applications are designed for different tasks.
topics.activity_text: Match Word, Paint and an educational app to the task each one helps complete.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Utility Software
topics.content: Utility software helps maintain, protect or manage a computer. The textbook gives antivirus software as an example of a utility program.
learning_points: Utility software performs maintenance tasks.
Antivirus software helps protect a computer from viruses.
Utilities support the smooth operation of a computer.
topics.activity_text: Discuss why keeping security software updated is a useful computer-care habit.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

chapters.title: File Management
chapters.description: Explore file management through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: Documents, pictures, audio and video can be stored as files.
A folder can contain files and other folders.
A document file stores written information.
A spreadsheet stores information in rows and columns.

topics.title: Files and Folders
topics.content: A file stores information created or used on a computer. Folders help organise files so that related information can be found easily.
learning_points: Documents, pictures, audio and video can be stored as files.
A folder can contain files and other folders.
Meaningful names make files easier to identify.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to suggest a folder structure for keeping school documents, pictures and projects organised.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Types of Files
topics.content: Files may contain different kinds of information. The textbook shows examples such as documents, spreadsheets, presentations, pictures, audio and video.
learning_points: A document file stores written information.
A spreadsheet stores information in rows and columns.
A presentation file contains slides.
Image, audio and video files store media.
topics.activity_text: Show file icons and ask students to match each one with its likely content.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Creating and Saving Files
topics.content: When students create work in an application, they should save it as a file in an appropriate folder. Saving preserves the work for later use.
learning_points: Choose Save or Save As from the application.
Select the folder where the file should be kept.
Enter a meaningful file name.
Save the file and remember where it is stored.
examples: Choose folder: Select where to store it.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate saving a practice document in a folder named Class Work.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Copying, Moving and Renaming Files
topics.content: File management includes organising files after they have been created. Copying makes another copy, moving changes the file location, and renaming changes its name.
learning_points: Copy creates an additional copy of a file.
Move places a file in another folder.
Rename changes the file name.
Check the destination before moving or copying important work.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate copying a sample file into another folder and renaming the copy.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Deleting and Restoring Files
topics.content: Unneeded files can be deleted. In Windows, deleted files may be placed in the Recycle Bin, where they can be restored before the bin is emptied.
learning_points: Select the file or folder you want to delete.
Use the Delete command.
Check the Recycle Bin if a deleted file is needed again.
Restore a file from the Recycle Bin when available.
topics.activity_text: Explain the difference between deleting a file and restoring it from the Recycle Bin.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

chapters.title: Fun with Paint
chapters.description: Explore fun with paint through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: Paint provides a drawing area or canvas.
The tools help draw, colour and edit pictures.
Pencil and brushes create freehand marks.
The eraser removes parts of a drawing.

topics.title: Introduction to MS Paint
topics.content: MS Paint is a drawing program used to create and edit pictures. The chapter introduces the Paint window and the tools used to make drawings.
learning_points: Paint provides a drawing area or canvas.
The tools help draw, colour and edit pictures.
The colour palette is used to choose colours.
topics.activity_text: Open Paint and ask students to identify the drawing area, tools and colour palette.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Paint Tools
topics.content: Paint provides tools such as pencil, brushes, eraser, fill with colour, text and shape tools. Each tool is used for a different drawing task.
learning_points: Pencil and brushes create freehand marks.
The eraser removes parts of a drawing.
Fill with Colour fills an enclosed area.
Text adds words to a picture.
Shape tools create ready-made shapes.
examples: Fill: Fill an area with colour.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to draw a simple house using line, rectangle, ellipse, brush and fill tools.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Drawing and Filling Shapes
topics.content: Shape tools help create neat geometric shapes. Students can choose a shape, draw it on the canvas and apply outline or fill options.
learning_points: Choose a shape from the Shapes group.
Drag on the canvas to draw the shape.
Use outline and fill choices to change its appearance.
Use colours to make the drawing clear.
topics.activity_text: Create a scene using rectangles, circles, lines and filled shapes.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Selecting, Cropping and Resizing Pictures
topics.content: Selection tools let users choose part of a picture. Cropping keeps the selected area, while resizing changes the picture dimensions.
learning_points: Use a selection tool to select an area.
Crop removes the parts outside the selected area.
Resize changes the picture size.
Review the picture after editing.
examples: Select: Choose part of a picture.
topics.activity_text: Demonstrate selecting a picture area, cropping it and resizing the result.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Saving a Picture
topics.content: After creating or editing a picture, save it so it can be opened later. Choose a suitable name and location for the picture file.
learning_points: Open the File menu and choose Save or Save As.
Choose a location and enter a file name.
Select an appropriate image format when prompted.
Save changes after editing.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to save their drawing in the Pictures folder with a meaningful name.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

chapters.title: Introduction to MS Word
chapters.description: Explore introduction to ms word through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: Word is used to prepare letters, reports and school assignments.
It provides tools to type and format text.
Start Word from the available program list or shortcut.
The Ribbon contains tabs and groups of commands.

topics.title: Introduction to MS Word 2016
topics.content: Microsoft Word 2016 is a word-processing program. It is used to create, edit, format and print text documents.
learning_points: Word is used to prepare letters, reports and school assignments.
It provides tools to type and format text.
Documents can be saved and printed.
examples: Document: A page of written work.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to name documents they could create using Word.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Starting Word and Its Window
topics.content: The chapter introduces how to start Microsoft Word and the main parts of its window, including the Ribbon, tabs, document area and status information.
learning_points: Start Word from the available program list or shortcut.
The Ribbon contains tabs and groups of commands.
The document area is where text is entered.
The title bar identifies the open document.
examples: Document area: Type and edit text.
topics.activity_text: Open Word and ask students to point out the title bar, Ribbon and document area.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Creating and Saving a Document
topics.content: A new Word document provides a blank page where users can type. Saving stores the document with a name in a chosen location.
learning_points: Create a blank document.
Type text in the document area.
Use Save or Save As to store the document.
Choose a clear file name and location.
examples: New document: Start a blank page.
topics.activity_text: Guide students to create a short paragraph and save it as My First Document.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Editing and Selecting Text
topics.content: Word allows users to select text and make changes. Editing includes inserting, removing, copying or moving text.
learning_points: Select text before applying many editing commands.
Backspace and Delete remove selected or nearby text.
Copy and Paste can duplicate text.
Undo can reverse a recent action.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to type a sentence, select one word, copy it and paste it elsewhere.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Opening and Printing a Document
topics.content: A saved document can be opened again for reading or editing. Word also provides print settings to produce a paper copy.
learning_points: Use Open to find and open a saved document.
Check the document before printing.
Choose the printer and required print settings.
Use Print to produce a hard copy.
topics.activity_text: Show students the Open and Print screens without printing unnecessary pages.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

chapters.title: Formatting in Word
chapters.description: Explore formatting in word through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: Select the text to be formatted.
Choose a font style.
Select the text first.
Open the Font Colour option.

topics.title: Changing Font and Font Size
topics.content: Font formatting changes the appearance of text. Font family and font size can be selected from the Font group on the Home tab.
learning_points: Select the text to be formatted.
Choose a font style.
Choose a suitable font size.
Use readable fonts and sizes for school documents.
topics.activity_text: Type a heading and change its font and size.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Changing Font Colour
topics.content: Font Colour changes the colour of selected text. Colour can help distinguish headings or highlight important words.
learning_points: Select the text first.
Open the Font Colour option.
Choose a colour from the palette.
Use colour carefully so that text remains readable.
examples: Selected text: Apply formatting to chosen words.
topics.activity_text: Format a heading in a different colour while keeping body text easy to read.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Bold, Italic and Underline
topics.content: Bold, Italic and Underline are basic text effects used to emphasise selected words or headings.
learning_points: Bold makes text appear heavier.
Italic slants text.
Underline draws a line beneath text.
Select the text before applying an effect.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to format one word in bold, one in italic and one underlined.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Text Alignment
topics.content: Alignment controls how paragraphs are positioned between the page margins. Word provides left, centre, right and justified alignment.
learning_points: Left alignment places text along the left margin.
Centre alignment centres text.
Right alignment places text along the right margin.
Justified alignment adjusts spacing so text lines meet both margins.
topics.activity_text: Create a heading and paragraph, then demonstrate the different alignment options.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Bullets, Numbering and Paragraph Spacing
topics.content: Bullets and numbering organise information into lists. Paragraph and line spacing control the space between lines and paragraphs.
learning_points: Bullets are useful for lists without a fixed order.
Numbering is useful for steps or ordered items.
Line spacing changes the space between lines.
Paragraph spacing adds space before or after paragraphs.
topics.activity_text: Format a short list of classroom rules using bullets, then format steps using numbering.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

chapters.title: Introduction to Coding
chapters.description: Explore introduction to coding through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: A program is a set of instructions.
Instructions must be arranged in a meaningful order.
ScratchJr uses visual blocks instead of requiring typed code.
Projects can include characters and a stage.

topics.title: What is Coding?
topics.content: Coding means writing instructions that a computer or digital device can follow. The chapter introduces programming through visual, block-based activities.
learning_points: A program is a set of instructions.
Instructions must be arranged in a meaningful order.
Coding blocks help beginners create programs by joining visual commands.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to give step-by-step instructions for moving from their desk to the classroom door.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Introduction to ScratchJr
topics.content: ScratchJr is a visual programming environment for young learners. It lets children create stories and simple games by connecting coding blocks.
learning_points: ScratchJr uses visual blocks instead of requiring typed code.
Projects can include characters and a stage.
Connected blocks tell a character what actions to perform.
topics.activity_text: Open ScratchJr and identify the stage, character and block palette.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: ScratchJr Window and Characters
topics.content: A ScratchJr project uses a stage, characters and coding blocks. Characters can be selected and arranged to create a scene.
learning_points: The stage displays the project.
Characters are the objects that perform actions.
A project can use more than one character.
Backgrounds help create the scene.
topics.activity_text: Create a new project, choose a character and select a background.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Using Coding Blocks
topics.content: Coding blocks are joined to form a sequence of instructions. Different block groups control events, movement, appearance, sound and other actions.
learning_points: Start or event blocks begin a script.
Motion blocks move a character.
Looks blocks change appearance.
Sound blocks play sounds.
Control blocks help manage the sequence of actions.
topics.activity_text: Connect a start block and movement blocks, then run the script to see the character move.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Creating and Running a Project
topics.content: A ScratchJr project is made by choosing a scene and characters, connecting coding blocks and running the program to observe the result.
learning_points: Choose a background and character.
Join blocks in the required order.
Run the project and observe the character.
Change the blocks and test the project again.
topics.activity_text: Create a short animation in which a character moves across the stage.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

chapters.title: Artificially Intelligent Gadgets
chapters.description: Explore artificially intelligent gadgets through clear explanations, examples and guided activities.
learning_objectives: AI systems can analyse information and respond to it.
Some AI devices recognise voices, images or movement.
Smart devices can respond to commands or changes in their environment.
Some devices help with home security and convenience.

topics.title: What is Artificial Intelligence?
topics.content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to computer systems and devices that perform tasks that normally require human-like abilities such as recognising patterns, understanding speech or making predictions.
learning_points: AI systems can analyse information and respond to it.
Some AI devices recognise voices, images or movement.
AI is used in smart gadgets and services described in the chapter.
examples: AI: Computer systems performing intelligent tasks.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to name a device that responds to voice, recognises a face or makes a recommendation.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: AI-Enabled Gadgets at Home
topics.content: The textbook describes smart home devices that use sensors, software and AI-related functions to respond to people and their surroundings.
learning_points: Smart devices can respond to commands or changes in their environment.
Some devices help with home security and convenience.
AI-enabled functions can make everyday devices more interactive.
topics.activity_text: Discuss examples of smart devices students may have seen at home.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Smart Speakers and Assistants
topics.content: Smart speakers and voice assistants respond to spoken commands. They can answer questions, provide information and control supported functions.
learning_points: A voice assistant can recognise spoken requests.
Smart speakers can respond with information or audio.
The textbook gives examples such as Alexa, Siri and Google Assistant.
examples: Smart speaker: Responds to voice commands.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to describe a voice command they might give to a smart assistant.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Smart Cameras and Other AI Devices
topics.content: AI-enabled cameras and other smart devices can analyse information from their sensors. The chapter introduces examples such as smart cameras, watches and other gadgets.
learning_points: A smart camera can detect or recognise activity.
A smart watch can track information such as movement or steps.
Different AI devices are designed for different tasks.
topics.activity_text: Match smart cameras, watches and other devices with the information they can detect or provide.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.

topics.title: Uses of AI in Everyday Life
topics.content: AI-enabled gadgets are used in everyday life for assistance, communication, security, entertainment and other tasks. The textbook highlights both home and personal devices.
learning_points: AI-enabled devices can make some tasks easier.
People should use smart devices responsibly and protect personal information.
AI devices assist people but do not replace human judgement and responsibility.
examples: Everyday use: Assist people with tasks.
topics.activity_text: Ask students to choose one AI gadget and explain how it helps people.
topics.study_note: This lesson explanation is adapted from the supplied Foundation 3 textbook. It is a learning aid, not a verbatim copy of the full textbook page. Use the textbook PDF for original diagrams, examples and complete activities.
